from PRESS.visualization import plot_ball_drive_risk

opendata = Path(os.environ.get("SKILLCORNER_OPENDATA", Path.cwd().parent / "opendata"))

press = PRESS.from_skillcorner(match_dir)

frame_id = 6955

plot_ball_drive_risk(press, frame_id)
plt.savefig("figures/vignette_01_drive_pitch.png", dpi=170)
plt.savefig("figures/vignette_01_drive_pitch.svg")

title: Ball-drive risk
text:
9. Scope and limitations
The model represents the carrier as a point moving at constant velocity over the hypothetical drive, with simplified defender turning and a reachability-gated tackle process. It does not represent body posture, foot-level ball control, individual skill or coordinated defensive behaviour. Probabilities for horizons shorter than one second follow from the survival formulation and have not been separately calibrated.

title: Ball-drive risk
text:
10. References and next steps
Bekkers (Bekkers 2025) motivates moving-target pressing and reachability. Spearman (Spearman et al. 2017; Spearman 2018) motivates arrival uncertainty and control rates. Fernández, Bornn and Cervone (Fernandez, Bornn, and Cervone 2019; Fernandez, Bornn, and Cervone 2021) motivate the canonical action decomposition. Stalpaert et al. (Stalpaert 2022) provide a carry-model benchmark, and Schepers et al. (Schepers et al. 2025) motivate the dribbling covariates. SkillCorner (SkillCorner 2026) motivates the interpretation of spatial constraints.
The equations above describe the PRESS formulation and do not reproduce any single cited model. Cohort selection, held-out results and comparisons are documented in the ball-drive benchmark. The pass-success component is described in the next model vignette.

title: Project roadmap
text: PRESS is a research project that combines a reusable inference package with documentation of its five fitted components, their evaluation and descriptive pressure reports. This page summarizes the completed work and possible research extensions.

title: Project roadmap
text:
Current state

Five fitted components: ball-drive risk, pass probability, pass selection, action selection and residual risk. The package includes the production refits. The active ball-drive solver is the final spline model.
Held-out evaluation: the benchmark pages distinguish match-level held-out predictions from production refits, describe fold-specific feature construction and report predictive metrics and calibration. The composed-risk benchmark evaluates h and xLoss separately from their component models.
Real-match examples and reports: model examples use observed tracking frames and package plots. The pressure report includes pressure escape, drawing pressure and sustained carrying, together with exposure summaries and expected-minus-observed failures per 100 elevated-risk actions. These summaries are descriptive.
User-facing API: the three-part user guide covers preprocessing, segmentation and an end-to-end real-match workflow. The reference is organized into initialization and classes, solvers, getters and plots. Match input tables have explicit contracts, and result exports can be saved and reloaded.
Spatial features: accessibility and value: BCOS and xT have separate definitions, examples and numerical or resolution checks.
Research pipeline: numbered feature, fitting, scoring and production-refit stages live in pipeline/. The pipeline page gives the dependency order, commands and output layout.

The training pipelines remain a work in progress and will continue to be revised after the initial release. Changes to estimation or validation procedures will be documented and accompanied by updated benchmark results.

title: Project roadmap
text:
Possible research extensions
Final BCOS in fitted predictors. The package provides the final transport-with-killing accessibility model. The existing action-selection and residual-risk benchmarks use a preliminary effective-hazard BCOS formulation. Recompute fold-specific BCOS features, retrain and repeat held-out evaluation with the final formulation before replacing the frozen classifier feature. The effective-hazard solver remains available until that evaluation is complete.
High-risk calibration and component performance. Investigate the High band of h in greater detail, separating limited-sample uncertainty from possible calibration errors in the passing and carrying branches. Review discrimination and calibration across the five individual tasks and their contribution to composed risk, retaining held-out evaluation and uncertainty estimates. Seek additional tracking-and-event datasets to expand the sample and assess whether the findings persist beyond the current ten matches, checking compatibility of action labels and outcome definitions before comparison or pooling.
A richer description of accessible space. Explore directional, radial and spatial summaries of the BCOS field beyond its total area. Their additional value for action selection and residual risk would need held-out evaluation. The current scalar already combines movement and defensive reachability; richer summaries should demonstrate useful information beyond the existing features.
Richer passing-option descriptors. Action selection and residual risk currently summarize the pass-selection and pass-probability maps by averaging over candidate destinations. When the available options have several distinct spatial modes, these averages may discard useful information. Evaluate features that describe the distribution and joint quality of passing options, such as prominent modes or probability mass across field regions, with fold-specific construction and held-out comparison against the current summaries.
Original carrier after a hypothetical turnover. In the failed-pass branch of action selection and residual risk, the opponent recovers the ball and the original carrier becomes one of the players it would face. Evaluate including the original carrier in the construction of his team’s pressure lines and counting him among the opponents in the player counts of that branch, since from the recovering team’s perspective he is part of the defensive structure. The current features exclude the original carrier from his own team’s line construction and from the counts in both pass-outcome branches. This extension would require recomputing the affected features, refitting and held-out comparison.
Consistent one-second reference for carrying features. In action selection and residual risk, teammate and opponent counts ahead of the carrier currently use the carrier’s present position, whereas carrying-related xT and pressure-line descriptors use the one-second projection. Evaluate moving the reference line for both counts to that same projected carrier position, retaining current player positions, the strict longitudinal comparison and the exclusion of the carrier. This would align the feature conventions and requires recomputing the affected features, refitting and held-out comparison.
More data and alternative predictors. Repeat the tree-model and training-only resampling comparisons on a larger sample, using Stalpaert as a methodological reference (Stalpaert 2022). The existing CatBoost experiment left the benefit of resampling open. A flexible model could use physical risk together with contextual features, while the present package retains the explicit ball-drive likelihood. More complex architectures, such as graph neural networks, are discussed in the modelling choices of the pipeline page.
Unobserved engagement and tactical information. Body orientation, foot-level control and individual skill are outside the current feature set. Seek 3D tracking or pose datasets with sufficient detail to study body orientation and player–ball interaction; the availability of suitable public datasets remains to be established. Richer video observations and models of collective defensive interaction could address other parts of this limitation. Larger samples would also permit stronger assessment across teams, competitions and match contexts. Such extensions require new evidence and validation.

Getters inspect existing inputs or outputs and return stored values. Tables and results are copied by default so editing a returned value does not alter the object.

title: Reference: getters and saved results
text:
Match, possessions and frames







Method
Return value and selection




get_xt_grid(frame_id=None)
Copy of the supplied/default xT map; with a frame ID, the map actually used by stored pass selection.


get_match_info()
Dictionary: input fps, pitch dimensions and optional match ID.


get_players(*, team_id=None)
Roster with internal IDs and optional original provider IDs/names. Team filter is home/away.


get_team_possessions(possession_id=None, *, team_id=None)
Explicit team intervals, optionally selected by team-possession ID and team. Always returns a DataFrame; omitted filters select all and unmatched filters return an empty table. Raises ValueError if no interval table was supplied.


get_player_possessions(possession_id=None, *, team_id=None, player_id=None, team_possession_id=None)
Individual intervals, optionally selected by individual possession ID, team, player or linked team interval.


get_actions(possession_id=None, *, team_id=None, player_id=None, team_possession_id=None, include_snapshots=False, valid_only=False)
Canonical pass/carry action intervals. Each frame_start is a checkpoint. Optional snapshots retain their noncanonical flag; valid_only=True selects usable start states.


get_frame(frame_id)
One wide tracking row as a DataFrame; unknown ID raises KeyError.


get_frames(possession_id=None, *, valid_only=False)
Sorted tracking, optionally inside a team interval. Includes both endpoints and in-flight rows.


get_player_frames(player_possession_id, *, valid_only=False)
Sorted tracking inside one individual interval.


get_state(frame_id)
Carrier, teammates, defenders, velocity arrays, IDs, direction and native pitch dimensions. Teammates/opponents have padded shapes (10,2) / (11,2). Missing carrier/direction or nonfinite carrier state raises ValueError.


get_frame_context(frame_id, *, granular=None)
Known current action origin/previous action; granular mode also includes completed one-second carries and elapsed time when recoverable. Default returns raw context independently of model loading; granular=False provides descriptive grouped categories.


get_elapsed_time(frame_id)
Elapsed individual-possession time in seconds, from annotations and fps. Raises ValueError when unavailable.



For get_player_possessions and get_actions, possession_id always identifies an individual possession. Omit it to select all possessions, or combine it with team_id="home" / "away" and the internal player_id. Filters are intersected. Use team_possession_id to restrict these tables to a team possession instead. IDs retain their input types; an unmatched filter returns an empty table.
get_team_possessions selects team intervals instead. Both possession getters always return DataFrames, even when selecting a single ID.
# Inspect the roster, then use its internal player_id.
players = press.get_players(team_id="home")
team_intervals = press.get_team_possessions(team_id="home")
possessions = press.get_player_possessions(player_id="home_8")
actions = press.get_actions(player_id="home_8")

# The same individual possession ID selects possessions and actions.
# Use an ID shown by get_player_possessions(); here, the user-guide example.
individual_id = "8_774"
possession = press.get_player_possessions(possession_id=individual_id)
actions = press.get_actions(possession_id=individual_id)
# Evaluate the actions at their starts: these are the canonical checkpoints.
usable_actions = press.get_actions(possession_id=individual_id, valid_only=True)
checkpoint_frames = usable_actions.frame_start.to_list()
valid_only checks for a known carrier, usable attack direction and finite carrier position/velocity, either in tracking frames or at action starts. It checks the usability of the state; observed terminal outcomes and benchmark cohort filters are separate. Those evaluation filters are documented in the benchmark.
Checkpoint sampling is separate from evaluating an arbitrary frame. Successful short control tails and terminal foul/clearance snapshots can be included for inspection; they stay outside the action-selection training examples. Prefer canonical action starts when forming a non-overlapping survival sequence.

title: Reference: getters and saved results
text:
Computed results
Component names are PPCF, BALL_DRIVE_RISK, ACTION_SELECTION, HAZARD, BCOS, RESIDUAL_RISK, XLOSS, case-insensitive. Aliases: PASS_RISK / PASS_SELECTION select PPCF, BALL_DRIVE selects BALL_DRIVE_RISK, H selects HAZARD, and RESIDUAL selects RESIDUAL_RISK. Unknown components raise ValueError; uncomputed or invalidated outputs raise KeyError.







Getter
Stored output




get_result(component, frame_id, *, copy=True)
One result mapping, copied by default. copy=False explicitly accesses the internal cache.


get_results(component=None)
Copied cache for a component, or all component caches.


get_ppcf_result(frame_id)
Compact weighted success/failure summaries, or detailed control/completion/choice maps and flight times; configuration and model references.


get_pass_selection_result(frame_id)
Grid, conditional destination probabilities and stored context.


get_ball_drive_risk_result(frame_id)
Total loss/survival; defender causes and survival curve when details are retained; configuration and model references.


get_action_selection_result(frame_id)
Native pass/carry probabilities, current feature record and model ID.


get_hazard_result(frame_id)
Hazard, automatically assigned band, Drive risk, destination-weighted Pass failure expected, and weighted pass success rppcf.


get_bcos_result(frame_id)
BCOS area; accessibility field, grid and interception diagnostics when details are retained; configuration reference.


get_residual_risk_result(frame_id)
Residual loss probability, observed elapsed time and model dependencies.


get_xloss_result(frame_id)
xLoss, local Hazard, conditional residual probability and model metadata.



After a complete risk calculation, the default outputs are compact: PPCF contains destination-weighted expected success/failure, ball-drive risk contains total loss/survival, BCOS contains its area, and the other components retain their scalar predictions. Spatial fields, defender causes and feature records in the table above require keep_details=True or separate component calculations.
The getters distinguish model, configuration and result. For ball drive, the fitted s, coefficients and spline transformations belong to the model; the defender v_max and integration step actually used belong to the configuration; the loss probability belongs to the frame result. For BCOS, the carrier and defender maximum speeds are configuration inputs and the area in m² is a result. The default dispersion is supplied by the ball-drive model.

get_result_configuration(frame_id, component=None) returns copied shared physical/numerical settings and model references after standalone or complete calls. Omit component to collect settings from all currently valid components; supply e.g. "BALL_DRIVE_RISK" to select one. The xT input is included once destination features have been calculated.
get_result_model(component, frame_id) returns the shared fitted model actually used, including custom parameters. PASS_SELECTION selects the destination model; PPCF/PASS_RISK selects the completion model. Inspect .parameters, spline bases or .to_dict(); use the latter for an editable copy.

clear_results(component=None, *, frame_ids=None) clears selected results and releases configurations/models no longer referenced by any retained result. Omitted component means all; omitted frames means all stored frames. Recomputing/clearing an upstream component invalidates its dependants: pass/drive changes invalidate destination choice, action choice, h, residual risk and xLoss; BCOS changes invalidate action choice onward. Recompute prerequisites before requesting a downstream output.

title: Reference: getters and saved results
text:
Saving and restoring
folder = press.save_results("outputs/match_results")
# Recreate the match from the same inputs and model settings:
other.load_results(folder)
save_results(path, *, overwrite=False) creates a directory with:

metadata.json: format version, match metadata, input/model fingerprints, shared calculation configurations, model manifests and the typed result structure;
arrays.npz: compressed numerical arrays, preserving shapes and dtypes.

It returns the directory as a Path. The export contains results, metadata and model manifests; raw tracking, tree weights and training outputs stay with their sources. Physical model parameters and bases are saved once in their model manifests. Tree manifests identify the installed/supplied weights; custom tree weights must also be available when restoring. The format is plain JSON and compressed arrays. Existing exports require overwrite=True.
load_results(path, *, overwrite=False) verifies the format, array checksum, input tables, frequency/pitch metadata and fitted model settings before changing the cache. A mismatching match/model or malformed export raises an error. Existing component/frame results require explicit overwrite. Recreating an object for loading requires the same annotations as well as the same tracking, because annotations affect model context.
For scalar possession summaries returned by compute_possession or compute_risk_player_possession, use normal DataFrame exports such as summary.to_csv(path, index=False) or to_parquet. Those summaries are distinct from full spatial fields.

title: Reference: initialization and classes
text:
The reference has four parts: 1 · Initialization and classes · 2 · Solvers · 3 · Getters and saved results · 4 · Plot functions.
PRESS represents one match. Input conversion, navigation, numerical inference, result storage and plotting are separate operations. Initialization copies and validates the supplied tables; models run only when requested. The five fitted models are shipped with the package and load lazily, ready to use without training.

title: Reference: initialization and classes
text:
Initialization
The constructor signature is:
PRESS(
    tracking_data,
    events_data=None,
    *,
    possessions_data=None,
    player_possessions_data=None,
    actions_data=None,
    fps=10.0,
    pitch_length=None,
    pitch_width=None,
    match_id=None,
    player_metadata=None,
    xT_grid=None,
    ball_drive_model=None,
    pass_risk_model=None,
    pass_selection_model=None,
    action_selection_model=None,
    residual_risk_model=None,
)
All arguments after events_data are keyword-only. Each model argument accepts a fitted model instance, its JSON-manifest path, or None for the installed pretrained model. Physical models also accept named parameter dictionaries, described below.

Canonical tracking contract
Positions are centred pitch metres; x spans [-length/2, length/2] and y spans [-width/2, width/2]. Velocities are m/s in those same axes. Data from a provider with another origin, scale or orientation must be converted first. The direct constructor uses the supplied values as they are: velocities and sampling come from the caller. The original-file SkillCorner loader prepares velocities explicitly, as described below.







Input
Required information




tracking_data
Wide DataFrame, one row per unique integer frame; ball_x, ball_y, player_possession, attacking_side; player columns <player_id>_x, _y, _vx, _vy.


Player IDs
Internal aliases home_<integer> / away_<integer>. The integer is an identifier that may differ from the shirt number. The carrier must name a player with tracking columns.


Optional speed
<player_id>_v is derived as hypot(vx,vy) only when absent. Supplied components are used as given.


Carrier and direction
Carrier can be missing in flight/no-control frames. Model evaluation needs an observed carrier and left_to_right or right_to_left. A plain frame plot also supports missing carriers.


Missing players
Missing XY observations can remain missing; physical states pad absent players internally. An observed player requires finite velocity. A team accepts at most eleven observed players.


fps
Actual input frequency in Hz, default 10. Consecutive integer frame IDs are sampling ticks; missing observations retain their original IDs. This is independent of the numerical solver steps.


Pitch dimensions
Explicit positive metre values, or constant pitch_length / pitch_width columns. If neither is supplied, defaults are 105 × 68 m. Conflicting explicit/input dimensions raise ValueError.


match_id
Optional match identifier, inferred from a single-valued tracking column if present. Each object holds a single match.


player_metadata
Optional roster keyed by unique internal player_id; may retain source IDs and names.



Observed player velocities must be finite (NaN or infinity raise an error). Missing players keep their missing positions. Large coordinates used for internal padding are excluded from pressure-line calculations and plots.


Possessions, actions and context



Table
Schema and purpose




possessions_data
Explicit team intervals: unique possession_id, team_id (home/away), inclusive integer frame_start, frame_end. Optional lost supports reporting. Team intervals are disjoint.


player_possessions_data
Alternative individual intervals, linked through verified successful passes. See the linking contract below. Supply either the individual or the team interval table.


actions_data
Inclusive intervals with frame_start, frame_end, action, start_type, previous_action. Optional possession_id, is_canonical, time_since_start and other annotations retain their meaning. When individual possessions are supplied and this table is omitted, PRESS constructs actions and checkpoints using its canonical convention. See Possession segmentation and context.


events_data
Optional canonical events with frame, player_id, team_id, event_type. Pass events additionally require boolean is_successful and an identified receiver for completions. Raw provider events must be adapted first.



Team possession and individual control are distinct. A completed pass can link two individual intervals inside one team possession. Each table is built from annotated intervals. Frame-level computation uses either table only when its necessary context is not supplied explicitly.
The individual linking helper is PRESS.utils.match.link_team_possessions(player_possessions). It takes the individual intervals and returns copied (team_intervals, player_intervals_with_team_possession_id). A successful link requires the same team, an identified matching recipient, reception at the next interval’s start and no recorded interruption.
The input requires player_id, frame_start, frame_end, end_type, pass_outcome, target_pass, frame_receipt and boolean loss, with disjoint intervals. possession_id is required when the constructor builds canonical actions and enables individual-ID getters. start_type supplies the control origin and is set to unknown when omitted. Optional period and game_interruption_after prevent linking across periods and stoppages.
Current-state context may include start_type_raw, previous_action_raw, match_clock_min and score_difference_prefix. Context inputs are limited to current-state information; future destinations, outcomes, remaining duration and final score are excluded. Individual elapsed time and completed one-second carries (completed_canonical_drives) are derived from annotated starts using fps. An unknown elapsed time stays unknown.

title: Reference: initialization and classes
text:
Original SkillCorner files
press = PRESS.from_skillcorner(match_dir, xT_grid=None)
The folder contains <match_id>_match.json, <match_id>_tracking_extrapolated.jsonl and <match_id>_dynamic_events.csv. The folder name supplies the match ID; pass match_id= when it differs. The loader calculates velocities, reads annotated individual controls, constructs canonical actions and prepares observed context in memory. It works directly from the original files and builds the action table itself. Its default input frequency is 10 Hz; optional model arguments select fitted models.

title: Reference: initialization and classes
section: Data already prepared by the caller
text:
Data already prepared by the caller
Pass canonical tables directly to PRESS(tracking_data, ...). Coordinate conversion and event–tracking synchronization precede initialization. If individual possessions are missing, reconstruct them from aligned events first; PRESS then constructs its actions and checkpoints during initialization:
from PRESS.io import segment_possessions

tracking, individuals, _, report = segment_possessions(
    tracking, events, fps=input_frequency, match_id=match_id,
)
press = PRESS(
    tracking, player_possessions_data=individuals,
    player_metadata=players, fps=input_frequency, match_id=match_id,
    pitch_length=length_metres, pitch_width=width_metres,
)
The segmenter takes canonical, already aligned tracking/events, returns in-memory tables; loading from paths happens elsewhere. Its reception_fallback_max_distance=1.5 is a distance in metres: if estimated reception control is absent, a start one frame before the receiver’s next synchronized actor event requires finite ball/receiver XY within this distance and a frame strictly after release. None disables that fallback. With include_unannotated_starts=False, a missing later actor event yields no reception start. Coherent recovery/tackle overlaps retain the outgoing tackle frame and start the winner’s next control at the following observed frame. The returned report records candidate checks, reconciliations and unresolved overlaps. Detailed segmentation rules. Individual possessions may also be prepared externally. When actions_data is omitted, the constructor builds actions and checkpoints from these individual intervals using PRESS.io.canonical_actions. An explicitly supplied action table remains supported.
For long player/ball/context tables, the optional PRESS.io.convert_long_tracking(...) helper returns (wide_tracking, roster). Rename columns, convert units and supply source team IDs explicitly; the returned roster retains source-to-internal aliases. Map any additional annotation identifiers with that roster before initialization. This conversion is independent of possession segmentation. Complete external data contract.
PRESS(...) accepts prepared canonical tables. The separate PRESS.io.segment_possessions(...) function reconstructs controls and actions when missing. Original SkillCorner files use PRESS.from_skillcorner(...); other provider loading and synchronization remain external. See the external data guide.

title: Reference: initialization and classes
text:
xT map input
Both initialization paths accept xT_grid= as a two-dimensional array of cell values. The first axis is longitudinal x and the second lateral y; the map is oriented towards positive-x attack and spans the whole pitch. Values must be finite and nonnegative. Resolution may differ from the bundled 10 × 6 grid.
press = PRESS.from_skillcorner(match_dir, xT_grid=my_xt_map)
# Or, for already prepared inputs:
press = PRESS(tracking_data, xT_grid=my_xt_map)
Omitting the map uses the fitted production surface. The supplied map is copied and used consistently by pass selection and action selection; residual risk reuses the resulting action feature record. xT is estimated separately, outside initialization. A frame-level xT_grid= overrides the object map for that calculation. get_xt_grid() returns a copy of the object/default map; get_xt_grid(frame_id) returns the map used by that frame’s pass selection. The fitted artifacts stay unchanged.

title: Reference: initialization and classes
text:
Model, configuration and result
PRESS separates the fitted model, the settings used to evaluate it, and the prediction for a particular frame.



Level
Contents
Concrete example
Where to inspect it




Model
Estimated parameters, spline design and transformations, fitted trees, feature encoding and calibration.
Ball-drive lambda_0, s, linear/spline coefficients and knots; pass-risk lambda_control, s and isotonic map; pass-selection trees and temperature.
get_result_model(component, frame_id) returns the shared model actually used. .parameters exposes named physical-model coefficients; .to_dict() returns a separate complete artifact.


Configuration
Physical and numerical settings actually used after overrides, and the xT input used for feature construction.
Defender maximum speed, accelerations, integration steps, forecast horizon, BCOS carrier maximum speed, grid and radius.
get_result_configuration(frame_id, component=None) returns copied settings after standalone or complete calls. Configurations are shared in press.result_configurations.


Result
Predictions and essential context at one frame, with a reference to the configuration.
Ball-drive loss, expected pass failure, P(pass), BCOS area, h, its band and xLoss; optionally spatial fields and diagnostics.
press.results[component][frame_id], preferably accessed through the result getters.



For example, setting physics_kwargs={"v_max": 6.5} in a ball-drive calculation changes the configuration, while keeping the fitted coefficients and spline bases. Setting model={"s": 0.35, "gamma_v": [0, 0, 0]} changes the model specification, inheriting the omitted coefficients and bases. The predicted loss for the chosen frame is the result. Both overrides apply to that call and leave the object’s default fitted model as it is.
A model artifact also records its default physical settings. The configuration records the settings actually used in a particular calculation. BCOS is a spatial descriptor and takes its default dispersion from the associated ball-drive model. Thus ball-drive s is a fitted model parameter, while the value supplied to BCOS is part of its physical configuration.
For the physical models, ball_drive_model and pass_risk_model also accept named parameter dictionaries. Missing entries inherit production values. Per-frame model={...} inputs inherit the constructor’s model when one was supplied, otherwise production. BallDriveModel.parameters and PassRiskModel.parameters expose copies with named values; from_parameters(dictionary, base=None) constructs a model explicitly. The full to_dict() / from_json() export format remains available for coefficients, bases and calibration together. Parameter keys and examples.
Complete risk calls calculate only the preliminary effective-hazard BCOS used in training the fitted trees, while the standalone compute_bcos() defaults to final transport.
Complete risk calls keep compact results by default, and keep_details=True also retains maps, defender contributions, feature records and integration diagnostics. This option affects storage only, and predictions are identical. Individual component calls retain details for step-by-step use, with physical/numerical settings in shared configurations too. Tree feature names, order and categories belong to the model, whereas feature values belong to the frame calculation: the named action feature record is retained for residual risk and detailed inspection, then discarded by compact complete calls. Calculation and storage options.

Component-specific movement settings









Component
Parameter
Production default
Applies to




Pitch control / pass probability
v_max
5.5 m/s
Teammates and opponents in the TTI used for receiver-based flight-time estimation and destination control. The passer is excluded from control allocation.


Ball-drive risk
v_max
7 m/s
Defenders. The carrier follows its observed tracking velocity, held constant over the forecast horizon.


BCOS
v_bc_max
6.6 m/s
Carrier transport, starting from its observed velocity and orientation.


BCOS
v_def_max
7 m/s
Intercepting defenders.



These are separate per-component settings. The movement routines preserve observed initial speeds above the nominal maximum. BCOS inherits dispersion and defender movement defaults from the ball-drive model associated with the object, with separate carrier defaults; explicit physics_args override them. A temporary override in compute_ball_drive_risk() applies to that component only, and BCOS keeps its own settings. Likewise, pitch-control physics applies to pitch control alone. Call signatures and parameter inputs.

title: Reference: initialization and classes
text:
Main classes



Class
Role and public entry points




PRESS
One-match facade. Computes and stores components through the solver methods, navigates annotations through getters, and saves/restores results.


MatchInfo
Immutable fps, pitch_length, pitch_width, optional match_id. to_dict() returns copied metadata.


BallDriveModel
Frozen physical/spline model. pretrained(), from_json(path), to_dict(), predict(...), predict_batch(...).


PassRiskModel
Frozen trajectory-MLE parameters and isotonic map. pretrained(), from_json(path), to_dict(), calibrate(p), predict_field(...), predict_from_times(...).


PassSelectionModel
Frozen categorical destination-choice model. pretrained(), from_json(path), to_dict(), build_features(...), predict_features(...).


ActionSelectionModel
Native binary pass/carry policy. pretrained(), from_json(path), to_dict(), build_feature_record(...), build_features(...), encode(...), predict_features(...).


ResidualRiskModel
Conditional terminal individual loss after a successful carry. Same artifact readers, features_from_action_record(...), build_features(...), encode(...), predict_features(...).


BCOS
Optional standalone spatial descriptor, imported from PRESS.spatial_features. compute_bcos(...) and get_result(...); alternatively use press.compute_bcos(...) to keep its output in the match cache.



Import fitted classes from PRESS.model. Tree readers validate their adjacent UBJ checksum, vocabulary and feature order. JSON and UBJ files are the pretrained models. Physical scales, calibration maps and xT surfaces come from the supplied artifact and are used as saved.
BCOSModel and BCOSConfig are exported by PRESS.model. BCOSModel.from_ball_drive() takes dispersion and defensive movement settings from the installed physical fit. Interception acts during waiting at the origin and movement along the route. predict accepts carrier (2,), defenders (D,2) and targets (M,2); predict_field constructs the clipped destination grid. ReservoirBCOSModel, exported from the same namespace, retains the alternative with protected waiting and the same input interface. The classes only evaluate saved parameters. Existing numerical helpers and frozen fitted artifacts remain in their current modules.

Standalone model array contracts







Method
Input → output




BallDriveModel.predict(r_defs, v_defs, x_bc, v_bc, *, horizon=1, physics_kwargs=None)
Defender positions/velocities (D,2), carrier (2,) → loss, survival, defender causes, times and metadata. predict_batch adds a leading state dimension.


PassRiskModel.predict_field(p_pos, p_vel, x_bc, targets, attacker_idx, ball_carrier_idx, *, physics_kwargs=None)
Players (P,2), targets (M,2) → player control (P,M), raw/calibrated attacking completion, flight times and metadata.


PassSelectionModel.build_features(**state)
Current state and target-wise raw control → full candidate feature matrix. predict_features(matrix, *, log_membership=None, calibrated=True) returns normalized destination probabilities.


ActionSelectionModel.build_feature_record(**state)
Current carrier/players, grid, destination choices, calibrated pass completion, drive loss (converted once to the drive_success_1s feature), BCOS and context → one feature dictionary. build_features encodes it; predict_features returns native P(pass).


ResidualRiskModel.features_from_action_record(record, *, time_since_start, action_model, action_carry_probability=None)
Current action record, observed elapsed time and matching action model → residual feature matrix, including native P(carry), optionally reused from the matching action prediction. predict_features returns terminal loss probability conditional on a successful carry.



The full state keyword contract of the two tree feature builders is documented in their Python docstrings and the action-selection model vignette. Contextual names and feature polarity retain their trained meaning: pass selection uses raw control and drive loss; action selection uses calibrated completion and drive success. Residual risk reuses the drive success of the action-selection record, and the composition of h and xLoss uses drive loss.

title: Reference: initialization and classes
text:
Package layout
PRESS/
  core/           match initialization, navigation, orchestration and result access
  io/             adapters, synchronization, segmentation and JSON/NPZ exports
  model/          fitted inference classes, feature builders and numerical solvers
  physics/        motion, arrival-time and ball-flight primitives
  spatial_features/ BCOS public facade
  utils/          current shared geometry, action-context and possession utilities
  visualization/  shared native-pitch plots
The fitted model classes require their current feature contracts; missing or unsupported artifacts raise an error. Research pipeline · Project plan.

title: Research pipeline
text:
The procedural research code is organized in pipeline/, separately from the inference package PRESS/. It prepares the observations, fits the five components, composes held-out h and xLoss, and produces the descriptive reports. This page gives the reading order, dependencies and input/output layout.
Download the research pipeline · Source and reading guide · Distributed objects · Roadmap
The archive contains the pipeline/ source tree, documentation and split/grid protocols. It prepares task inputs from public SkillCorner match files and connects each fitted stage to its downstream tasks. Match data and fitted fold objects are generated during execution; the package supplies the final pretrained inference models.

title: Research pipeline
text:
Numbered workflow
The execution plan prints the commands in dependency order. The task scripts retain the same simple organization: definitions of covariates or likelihood, training and validation, then a pipeline that executes those steps.



Step
Component
Reading order




01
Preprocessing
Preparation → pipeline. Tracking derivatives and segmentation are in tracking.py; pass links are in passes.py.


02
Expected threat
Model → training → pipeline.


03
Physical ball-drive risk
Model and priors → training → pipeline.


04
CatBoost ball-drive comparison
Features → training → pipeline.


05
Pass probability
Physical model → training → pipeline.


06
Pass selection, flat and cross-nested
Features → training → pipeline.


07
Action selection, then residual risk
Features → training → pipeline.


08
h, xLoss and band evaluation
Composition → scores and bootstrap → pipeline.


09
Possession patterns and reports
Classification → scores → real-frame cases → pipeline.


10
Statistical summaries
Parameter and performance tables.



Flat and cross-nested pass selection share their feature calculation. Action selection and residual risk also share feature definitions, but their models, labels and outputs remain separate. The physical ball-drive model remains the deployed one; CatBoost is a benchmark comparison.

title: Research pipeline
text:
Modelling choices
Two considerations guide the choice of models. The analysis rests on ten matches, which favours simple models with few parameters. The project is also a research project, and in several components an exploratory choice was preferred to the search for the best predictive performance.
More complex architectures, such as the graph neural networks that SkillCorner uses for xLoss, would probably require a dataset of a different scale. This is a hypothesis based on the scale of the datasets typically used for such models; no feasibility study has been carried out.

title: Research pipeline
text:
Inputs and outputs
pipeline/
  00_pipeline.py
  frame_states.py
  inputs/                         # fixed split/grid protocols and report cases
  <component>/                    # source files in the table above
  outputs/                        # a new run's generated objects
    preprocessing/matches/<id>/   # tracking, events and segmented possessions
    preprocessing/task_inputs/    # observations and upstream models by task
    expected_threat/
    ball_drive/physical/
    ball_drive/catboost/
    pass_probability/
    pass_selection/flat/
    pass_selection/cnl/
    binary_classification/action_selection/
    binary_classification/residual_risk/
    composed_risk/
    reports/
    statistics/
Each model stores feature tables or physical arrays separately from fold fits, scores and production refits. Saved trees, spline bases, posterior quantities and calibration objects have explicit task folders. The pipelines preserve completed outputs; a fresh pipeline execution should use a new output root. The input/output guide describes the individual files.
The raw-data adapter reads the public SkillCorner match files. Shared preprocessing retains the broad observations and quality flags; task-specific outcome filters remain beside the task. Reconstructed task cohorts are saved under outputs/preprocessing/task_inputs/. Segmentation and context-label meanings are explained in the User guide.

title: Research pipeline
text:
Dependencies between models
Fold-specific feature builders receive explicit upstream model artifacts from the matching split. Held-out evaluation uses the models of the matching split. The handoff code exports completed physical, xT and choice fits into outputs/preprocessing/task_inputs/<task>/upstream/fold_<f>/; production counterparts are under upstream/production/. It checks the six-fitting/two-validation/two-test match roles before downstream feature extraction.
For the six-fitting/two-validation/two-test tree-model splits, physical and xT features use the matching fitting data; pass-completion and pass-selection calibration retain their declared validation roles. Residual-risk training uses cross-fitted P(carry); validation and test use the corresponding main action-selection model. Production residual training uses the five eight-fit/two-held action fits. The general benchmark and individual benchmark pages describe these procedures.
BCOS quantities used in the accepted benchmarks and pretrained classifiers come from the preliminary formulation with effective hazards. The transport-with-killing formulation is implemented and is the default for standalone BCOS calculations. Downstream retraining with this formulation remains planned. The training pipeline and pretrained classifiers preserve the preliminary benchmark feature definition.
For pass probability, the released source preserves the benchmark’s selection of one trajectory estimator per fitting split. It prepares both candidate paths, compares their reconstruction errors on the fitting matches, and uses the selected method for that fit. The pass-probability guide explains the procedure.

title: Research pipeline
text:
Composed risks, bands and reports
The composition stage produces one held-out h and xLoss per verified canonical checkpoint, using the models of the fold in which the match was held out. It combines the held-out predictions of the components.

Overall h/xLoss metrics and calibration use 15,085 verified-outcome states.
Bands, possession patterns and player/team reports use 14,919 states from 7,265 possessions with terminal canonical-action coverage.
Band intervals resample whole matches, with 2,000 replicates, fixed predictions/thresholds and seed 20261030. Empty and nearly empty bands are checked explicitly.
Player/team E−O scores resample whole individual possessions. The reports also provide pattern shares and exposure/retention summaries with their stated denominators.
Case studies retain real match/possession keys and use the package’s frame plotting function. A later verified control illustrates the outcome without adding a canonical checkpoint.

Details and results are in the composed-risk benchmark and the pressure report.

title: Research pipeline
text:
Local checks
The verification plan covers syntax and command-line entry points, reconstruction of a real match, physical calculations, short model fits, serialization, composition, metrics and report counts. The check guide explains their scope.
For pass selection, the short real-data check retains the complete destination grids for ten observed passes. It exercises flat/CNL likelihoods and gradients, the declared curvatures, reduced screening, tree and nesting updates, early stopping, temperature scaling, held-out scoring, feature importance and model export.
# Print the ordered research commands without executing fits.
python pipeline/00_pipeline.py --output-root /path/to/new_run

# Print checks; add --execute to run selected checks.
python pipeline/checks/run.py --output /path/to/new_checks

title: Research pipeline
text:
Release contents
The release script uses an explicit file allowlist. Alongside the source code, the site exposes statistical summaries of physical parameters, performance/calibration, bands and selected case-study/report tables. Full input tables, feature matrices, fold boosters, posterior objects and bootstrap replicates stay outside the release, and pretrained inference models are distributed with the PRESS package.

title: 4.1 · Use with other providers: data and preparation
text: This is part 4.1 of the User guide. PRESS evaluates a match in a provider-independent representation. Original SkillCorner files can be loaded directly with PRESS.from_skillcorner(...). For another provider, map identifiers and coordinates explicitly, align events to tracking, then supply or reconstruct individual possessions. PRESS constructs canonical actions and checkpoints from those intervals. See the Köln–Bayern example.

title: 4.1 · Use with other providers: data and preparation
text:
Tracking and match metadata
Positions use metres, centred at the pitch centre: x is longitudinal and y lateral. Velocities use m/s in those same axes. PRESS keeps the supplied direction, so state the ball carrier’s attacking direction at each frame. fps is the input sampling frequency; the models’ numerical integration steps remain fixed.








Information
Canonical fields
Requirement and consequence of absence




Match and sampling
match_id (string), fps (positive float)
Match identifier is optional for isolated inference. Correct fps is mandatory for segmentation, elapsed time and checkpoint spacing.


Pitch
pitch_length, pitch_width (positive metres)
Supply actual dimensions; the constructor retains its 105 × 68 m default when omitted.


Frame key
frame (unique integer)
Mandatory. Consecutive IDs must represent consecutive samples; gaps must retain their missing IDs.


Period
period (integer/string identifier)
Mandatory for segmentation and period-relative synchronization. Period means a half or an extra-time period.


Player identity
home_<integer> or away_<integer>
Mandatory, stable within match. Numbers are aliases that may differ from shirt numbers. Preserve provider IDs in player metadata.


Player state
<player>_x, _y, _vx, _vy (numeric)
Observed players require finite position/velocity. Absent players remain missing; PRESS pads numerical states internally. At most eleven observed players per team.


Carrier
player_possession (alias or missing)
Mandatory to evaluate a frame. Must be annotated or estimated explicitly upstream, since PRESS takes the carrier from this field.


Direction
attacking_side: left_to_right or right_to_left
Mandatory for the contextual models and field geometry. Reliable recovery requires information beyond a single frame.


Ball
ball_x, ball_y; optional ball_z
XY required by the match interface and real-frame plots. Z is needed for observed 3D launch fitting in training; production field predictions use XY only.


Clock and score
match_clock_min, score_difference_prefix
Required contextual information for a complete observed feature record. Numeric missing values are accepted by the fitted trees, and differ from known values. Score difference is carrier-team minus opposition, using only prior confirmed goals.


Player metadata
player_id, optional source IDs, name, goalkeeper flag
Optional for physical inference; role is needed to reproduce outfield-only evaluation cohorts. Take role from provider metadata or annotations.



For long data, use convert_long_tracking(players, ball, context, home_team=..., away_team=...). Player rows require frame, team_id, player_id, x, y, vx, vy; ball rows require frame, x, y; context requires frame, player_possession, attacking_side. team_possession disambiguates carrier IDs reused between teams. The returned roster records the alias mapping.
map_columns(table, {source: canonical}) renames fields. to_pitch_coordinates(...) converts declared coordinate bounds and optional velocity components. Both rely on the units and orientation declared by the caller. differentiate(...) is available when velocities must be reconstructed: derivatives are calculated separately on finite contiguous runs within each period. The filtering window must be stated by the caller.

title: 4.1 · Use with other providers: data and preparation
text:
Event information
normalize_events accepts a DataFrame with unique event_id, event_type, and either frame, UTC-compatible datetime, or period plus time_seconds. A supplied mapping translates provider event labels to the canonical event vocabulary. Unsupported event types become unknown; their source label is retained in original_event.








Event/attribute
Needed for
Missing information




Actor and team: player_id, team_id
Release, recovery and terminal action identification
Actorless administrative events are retained as administrative entries of the preprocessing audit.


Time and period; optional event XY
Event–tracking synchronization
Time links alone provide nearest-timestamp matching; release/contact refinement uses event XY and type-specific tracking information through an external synchronizer.


pass, is_successful (nullable boolean), receiver_player_id
Pass release, successful reception and verified pass links
Missing success stays unknown. A successful pass without an identified, observed receiver has an unverified endpoint.


recovery, interception, tackle; annotated winner where available
Control origin and direct possession loss
An annotated control acquisition can establish a start. Contact or a change of estimated controller alone does not establish a verified loss. Provider-specific tackle outcomes must identify what was won and by whom.


restart_type: open_play, throw_in, corner, free_kick, goal_kick, unknown
Reception/interception context
Reconstruct from the preceding pass and its restart qualifier. If unavailable, use unknown.


shot
Terminal action and shot-ending cohort exclusion
Without shot labels, the published no-shot cohort cannot be reproduced.


foul_suffered, clearance
Separate noncanonical terminal actions
Both remain terminal actions separate from individual loss. Omission can leave the endpoint unknown.


stoppage, restart
Prevent linking across interrupted play
Missing interruption information weakens endpoint verification and should be reported.


OBE and reliable endpoint annotations
Reproduce the published outcome-validation filters
Providers supply these in varying degree, and the outcome labels must come from annotated on-ball engagement or validated loss outcomes.



The public raw context categories are pass_reception, pass_interception, recovery, keep_possession, and reception/interception variants prefixed with throw_in, corner, free_kick, or goal_kick. ball_drive is additionally a previous-action category. unknown is accepted by the unchanged trained categorical vocabularies. The adapter infers keep_possession only with supporting annotation. Other unseen categories use the fitted unseen bucket.

title: 4.1 · Use with other providers: data and preparation
text:
Synchronization and segmentation
The separate synchronize_events(...) helper can validate supplied frame links or find nearest timestamps within periods. Event-specific release/contact refinement remains a separate step. Keep provider loading and alignment in the external preprocessing workflow: synchronization and individual-possession boundaries may be prepared outside PRESS, and canonical action segmentation follows the PRESS convention. Tracking and events must share canonical identifiers and synchronized frame links before segmentation; the segmenter verifies the links, and time alignment happens upstream.
For already prepared data, initialize PRESS(tracking_data, ...) directly. Supplied individual possessions are used as they are: initialize PRESS(tracking, player_possessions_data=individuals, ...) without actions_data, and PRESS constructs the canonical action table and checkpoints internally with canonical_actions(...). If individual intervals are missing, call segment_possessions(tracking, events, fps=..., match_id=...) first. It returns (tracking, individual_possessions, actions, report); pass the tracking and individual-possession tables to the constructor.
The segmenter uses synchronized actor events and the supplied carrier stream. Direct event links establish the eligible starts and terminal actions; clock-interpolated audit links do not establish these boundaries. A reception is located at an observed control frame or, when control is missed, at the fallback candidate described below, and each pass link is cross-checked against estimated control and flagged with outcome_verified. include_unannotated_starts=False restricts starts to successful receptions and annotated recoveries/interceptions, as in the IDSSE example. The default True additionally admits tracking-only starts and opponent control after failed passes; their boundary source is recorded.
A missed receiver control can use the frame immediately before the receiver’s next synchronized actor event when the observed ball–receiver XY distance is at most reception_fallback_max_distance (default 1.5 m). The candidate must exist in the same period and strictly follow release; unavailable coordinates or an inconsistent distance cannot support the fallback. Set the parameter to None to disable it. reception_fallback_checks records the tested candidates and reasons.
A recovery/interception overlapping the outgoing carrier’s tackle loss is reconciled only when winner/loser identities and adjacent relevant events support the same transfer. The outgoing end remains at the synchronized tackle frame and the incoming start moves to the next observed frame in that period. Original frames and event IDs remain recorded in overlap_reconciliations and the interval table. Other overlaps are reported without creating another interval.
The resulting intervals do not overlap or cross periods and missing tracking ranges. Terminal events preserve their football meaning: a foul suffered or clearance differs from direct loss, and a change of estimated controller without an eligible terminal event leaves the ending unknown. Original estimated control is retained separately from the carrier assigned to each reconstructed interval.
Provider annotations determine which events can support these labels. The IDSSE segmentation rules specify the starts, the reception search, the terminal events and tackle-winner rule, foul deduplication, clearance qualifier, pass-link verification and unknown-outcome handling for the Bundesliga example. Other providers need an equivalent semantic mapping, and each event meaning must be supported by the provider’s annotations.
Actions follow the existing canonical segmentation conventions: successful whole one-second carries; a failed final carry even when shorter than one second; and a pass-release checkpoint. Short successful tails are noncanonical exposure snapshots. Foul, clearance and shot endings remain outside the terminal pass/carry choices. previous_action uses the control’s origin before the first whole carry, then ball_drive. time_since_start is computed from actual frame differences and fps.
Keep the external event audit and segmentation report alongside the input tables. The direct constructor receives prepared tracking, individual intervals and metadata; an action table is optional. The original SkillCorner loader additionally exposes its raw dynamic-event audit through get_preprocessing_events() and its loading report through get_preparation_report(). Export input/audit tables separately from numerical result exports.

title: 4.1 · Use with other providers: data and preparation
text:
Requirements by model







Calculation
Minimum information beyond its fitted artifact




Ball-drive risk
Carrier and defender positions/velocities, native pitch dimensions. Inference needs the state only.


Pitch control/pass probability
Team identity, player positions/velocities, carrier and candidate destinations. The production flight model works from the current state.


Pass selection
The physical fields, xT, carrier state and contextual features. Missing categorical information has explicit fitted buckets.


BCOS
Carrier and defender positions/velocities; pitch dimensions and chosen destination domain.


Action selection and h
Preceding fields/choices, BCOS model feature, context and completed-carry count. The count needs a control start or an explicit supplied value.


Residual risk and xLoss
The same state plus action selection and observed elapsed individual-control time. Only past and current information is used.


Published validation/report cohorts
In addition: matched control endpoints, identified pass links, terminal action/outcome, interruptions, role and OBE where required. Missing annotations prevent reproducing that evaluation cohort.



Interoperability means that the same mathematical models can evaluate a mapped state; calibration and predictive validity on a new league, provider or segmentation system require separate evidence.

title: 4.1 · Use with other providers: data and preparation
text:
IDSSE preprocessing
The standalone preprocessing scripts load Sportec metadata and map provider semantics. The DataBallPy bridge runs separately from PRESS and exports portable Parquet tables. It was executed with DataBallPy 0.7.3; the bridge checks that API version explicitly. Other synchronizers can supply the same canonical interface.
The example uses event-anchored starts (include_unannotated_starts=False), DataBallPy’s event-order-preserving alignment and its tracking-based control estimate. Its control parameters are explicit: 1.5 m possession zone, 5 m/s ball-speed threshold, 10° ball-angle threshold and zero minimum possession-zone frames. Unsupported events may receive a separately labelled clock interpolation only between nearby aligned anchors in one period. A synchronization certainty score is an uncalibrated indicator. The resulting possessions are tracking-based estimates.
IDSSE is provided by the Deutsche Fußball Liga (DFL) under CC BY 4.0; cite Bassek et al. and credit the DFL (Bassek et al. 2025; German Sport University Cologne, n.d.). Obtain original files through the official repository’s data link. This project supplies code and selected derived figures. DataBallPy is a separate MIT-licensed dependency (Oonk, Grob, and Kempe 2026; Oonk and Grob, n.d.).

title: Residual risk benchmark
text:
Model and example · All benchmarks
The residual-risk model estimates, for a successful one-second carry, the probability that the individual possession ends in a terminal loss. A failed terminal pass, a direct possession loss or a clearance is labeled loss, and a completed terminal pass or a foul suffered is labeled no loss; the verification conventions are given in the evaluation cohort. The model vignette introduces the conditional terminal-outcome task, its likelihood, the relationship to the action-selection features, feature importance and an executable example. This benchmark documents the outcome conventions, the cohort, the training protocol, the predictive evaluation and the final fit. The classifier is a native XGBoost model with a binary logistic objective (Chen and Guestrin 2016).

title: Residual risk benchmark
text:
1. Evaluation cohort
Successful canonical one-second carries are identified as described in Possession segmentation and context. Each eligible state is a completed one-second carry within an outfield player’s individual possession, and shorter interrupted tails are excluded. The target is the terminal outcome of that individual possession.
Terminal outcomes are verified with the same conventions as Pass Selection and Ball Drive: terminal passes require verified continuous direct reception, and direct possession losses follow the OBE verification of the physical carry model. Terminal passes are retained irrespective of duration, curvature or unknown context. A failed terminal pass or a direct possession_loss is labeled loss (\(Y=1\)), and a completed terminal pass is labeled no loss (\(Y=0\)). Individual possessions ending in a clearance (\(Y=1\)) or a foul suffered (\(Y=0\)) are also included, while those ending in a shot are excluded. Clearances are treated as terminal losses under the assumption that they are induced by defensive pressure.
The cohort contains 7,820 successful one-second carry states, of which 1,423 end in a terminal individual loss (18.20%), across ten matches and 3,975 individual possessions. A possession can contribute more than one state.

Effective task-specific exclusions
The conditional target starts from 8,672 successful canonical one-second carry states in the broad action cohort. Terminal-outcome verification removes 14 states from 10 loss-ending parents without a valid associated OBE, and 838 states from 452 parents whose terminal pass is absent from the verified continuous direct-receipt cohort. All eligible states belonging to an affected parent are removed together. The two groups are disjoint, leaving 7,820 states from 3,975 individual possessions.
This target requires an observed successful full second, so the conditional training set consists of successful canonical carries. Completed passes, failed passes, clearances and fouls retain the labels shown above, with terminal passes of any flight duration or curvature.

title: Residual risk benchmark
text:
2. Model specification and features
The model uses 31 features: the action-selection feature family with two changes. The number of completed carries is replaced by the elapsed time since individual control began, and the carry probability \(P(\mathrm{carry})=1-q(s)\), with \(q(s)=P(A=\mathrm{pass}\mid s)\) the pass-choice probability of action selection, is added. The shared feature definitions are in the action-selection vignette. For this task \(P(\mathrm{carry})\) is cross-fitted, so that every state is scored by an action-selection model that did not see its match. The procedure is described in the next section.

title: Residual risk benchmark
text:
3. Model selection and validation
The evaluation uses five match-disjoint outer folds with 6 fitting + 2 validation + 2 test matches. The two validation matches remain fixed throughout each outer fold. They support upstream calibration and downstream grid/early-stopping selection, and the test matches are used only for evaluation. The six-match fit is evaluated directly on the test matches.
The XGBoost grid covers maximum depth (3, 4, 6, 8), minimum child weight (1, 5, 20), L2 regularization (0.1, 1, 3, 10) and learning rate (0.03, 0.05, 0.10), giving 720 fits for the reported 31-feature model, which includes \(P(\mathrm{carry})\). Row and column subsampling are 0.8, training allows at most 2,000 trees, and early-stopping patience is 100. Validation cross-entropy selects the configuration and the tree prefix before testing. Training uses the standard logistic objective on the original class frequencies, and the retained model returns native probabilities.

Cross-fitted P(carry)
Action selection learns the observed pass/carry labels on many of the same carry checkpoints that enter residual-risk training. It is also a flexible tree model. Using its in-sample predictions could therefore make \(P(\mathrm{carry})\) artificially confident on those observations; omitting their match reduces this source of bias in the learned feature. The physical ball-drive model shares carry checkpoints but has a more constrained parameterization. The pass-probability and pass-selection models are fitted on pass observations, with less direct overlap with residual-risk carry checkpoints. This makes \(P(\mathrm{carry})\) the priority for an additional cross-fitting step.
Cross-fitting is applied at the action-classifier layer: the action classifier that scores a fitting state omitted its match. Within each outer fold, training states are scored by three action-selection refits, each fitted on four of the six training matches with the XGBoost parameters of the fold and omitting the other two, and validation and test states are scored by the action-selection model of the same outer fold. These inner refits change the action-classifier weights only. Their physical, pass-choice, xT and BCOS inputs remain frozen from the outer six-match feature stack. The upstream features keep their outer-fold fits at this stage, so training-row predictions from those components can still be in-sample with respect to their own fits.

title: Residual risk benchmark
text:
6. Production model
The production model is a native 118-tree refit on all 7,820 eligible states. Depth 4, minimum child weight 5, L2 1 and learning rate 0.03 minimize the mean validation cross-entropy across the five grids. The best tree prefixes of this configuration in the five folds are 118, 133, 251, 87 and 92, and their median, 118, fixes the refit length.
The production residual-risk model is trained on out-of-fold values of \(P(\mathrm{carry})\), obtained as follows. The action-selection model is trained on eight of the ten matches, with the hyperparameters and number of trees selected for production action selection, and predicts \(P(\mathrm{carry})\) for the two remaining matches. Repeating this five times, so that every pair of matches is predicted once, gives a \(P(\mathrm{carry})\) value for every training state of residual risk. The residual-risk model is then fitted on all ten matches using these values. At inference on new data, \(P(\mathrm{carry})\) comes from the production action-selection model, trained on all ten matches.

title: Residual risk benchmark
text:
7. Discussion and limitations
Body orientation and posture are unavailable in this 2D tracking dataset, and the features use velocity direction in place of a measured body orientation (see Gu et al. above). The features summarize current carrier motion, tactical configuration and passing opportunities; full recent trajectories and explicit pairwise histories, as used by recurrent and graph-based action-rate models (Dick and Brefeld, above), are outside the feature set.

title: Residual risk benchmark
text:
8. Supplementary resources
For reproducibility, the metrics, selected configurations, fold scores, per-match scores, remaining-time diagnostic, literature locators, feature-importance analysis and refit provenance are provided as supplementary resources.

title: Pass selection benchmark
text:
Model and example · All benchmarks
The pass-selection model gives the probability of each candidate destination, conditional on a pass attempt. A shared XGBoost ensemble produces a utility for every destination, and a softmax turns the utilities into a categorical choice distribution. We also evaluate an exploratory cross-nested logit (CNL) that groups destinations probabilistically by potential receiver. The model vignette introduces the choice model, its predictors and an executable example. The likelihood-based tree learning follows RUMBoost (Salvadé and Hillel 2025).

title: Pass selection benchmark
text:
1. Evaluation cohort
The evaluation contains 6,810 decisions across ten SkillCorner matches, of which 1,009 are unsuccessful passes. Passers are outfield players. Unsuccessful passes are kept because destination choice is defined independently of completion. The observed endpoint is assigned to the nearest cell centre of the one-metre pitch grid, and all candidate cells enter the categorical normalization. The pooled uniform-choice reference cross-entropy is 8.873286.

Effective task-specific exclusions
The transition candidate base applies the shared verified-pass-link criteria, a usable release state and its positive flight-duration limit below ten seconds. These criteria leave the 6,810 decisions. Effective exclusion counts.
The cohort contains every pass of the final pass-probability cohort and also the passes shorter than 0.5 s. Destination choice uses the decision state and a hypothetical destination field, so the five initial ball observations used to reconstruct the observed flight, and the 0.5 s lower limit that they require, apply only to the pass-probability task.

title: Pass selection benchmark
text:
2. Model specification and features
The model uses 19 numerical predictors and two one-hot encoded contextual variables (50 encoded columns). Definitions and groups are given in the model vignette. Pitch control enters in its raw form, and the observed receiver and outcome are excluded.

Choice specifications and learning
For decision \(i\), let \(\mathcal G_i\) be the candidate destination cells, \(y_i\) the observed destination and \(z_{ij}\) the features of cell \(j\). Both specifications use one shared XGBoost ensemble, \(u_{ij}=f_\psi(z_{ij})\), to score all alternatives. They differ in the map from utilities to probabilities, and therefore in the derivatives used to fit the ensemble.


Flat multinomial logit
The deployed specification applies a softmax:
\[
\pi_{ij}=\frac{\exp(u_{ij})}{\sum_{k\in\mathcal G_i}\exp(u_{ik})}.
\]
The ensemble minimizes the categorical negative log-likelihood
\[
\mathcal L(\psi)=-\sum_i\log \pi_{i,y_i}(\psi),
\]
with utility gradient \(g_{ij}=\pi_{ij}-\mathbf 1\{j=y_i\}\). This is a single categorical likelihood over destinations: the probability of each cell depends on the utilities of all cells in the same decision.


Exploratory cross-nested logit
The CNL keeps the same utility function and lets each destination belong fractionally to several receiver nests, one per eligible teammate other than the carrier. Membership \(\alpha_{ijm}\) is proportional to teammate \(m\)’s individual raw pitch control at destination \(j\), normalized over eligible teammates (a zero-control destination gets uniform membership). Memberships are fixed by the physical state.
A single dissimilarity parameter \(\mu\in[0.1,1]\) (\(\rho\in[1,10]\)) is shared by all nests, because teammate identities and nest compositions change from decision to decision and teammate-specific scales would not be comparable. With \(\rho=1/\mu\), define
\[
S_{im}=\sum_{j\in\mathcal G_i}(\alpha_{ijm}e^{u_{ij}})^\rho,
\qquad
\pi_{ij}=\sum_m
\underbrace{\frac{S_{im}^{1/\rho}}{\sum_l S_{il}^{1/\rho}}}_{\text{nest probability}}
\underbrace{\frac{(\alpha_{ijm}e^{u_{ij}})^\rho}{S_{im}}}_{\text{destination within nest}}.
\]
At \(\mu=1\) the CNL reduces to the flat softmax. For \(\mu<1\) it relaxes the independence-of-irrelevant-alternatives restriction of the flat model, allowing more structured substitution among destinations tied to the same receiver.
Both models minimize the same observed-choice negative log-likelihood. For the CNL, probabilities, gradients and curvature are computed from the CNL probability function. In both cases XGBoost receives one gradient and one scalar curvature per candidate.


Iterative XGBoost estimation
The estimation follows RUMBoost (Salvadé and Hillel 2025), adapted to XGBoost and a single shared utility ensemble (the RUMBoost reference implementation uses LightGBM). The same ensemble \(f_\psi\) is evaluated on every candidate. Tree construction and regularization follow Chen and Guestrin (Chen and Guestrin 2016). Ensembles start from zero utilities, and the CNL also starts at \(\mu=1\).
At boosting iteration \(t\), the current utilities \(u_{ij}^{(t)}\) define a full probability distribution over the destinations of each pass. The loss of the observed choice, \(\ell_i=-\log \pi_{i,y_i}\), gives the direction in which utilities should move: alternatives with too much probability receive positive gradients, and the chosen destination receives a negative gradient in the flat model.
XGBoost then fits a regression tree \(b_t\) to a second-order approximation of the loss, using the gradients \(g_{ij}=\partial\ell_i/\partial u_{ij}\) and curvatures \(h_{ij}\) of the candidate rows. For a leaf \(A\) with \(G_A=\sum_{(i,j)\in A}g_{ij}\) and \(H_A=\sum_{(i,j)\in A}h_{ij}\), the leaf output is the standard
\[
w_A^*=-\frac{G_A}{H_A+\lambda}.
\]
The tree is added to the utility function shared by all destinations, with learning rate \(\eta\):
\[
u_{ij}^{(t+1)}=u_{ij}^{(t)}+\eta\,b_t(z_{ij}).
\]
Because the update changes the probabilities of all destinations in a pass, gradients and curvatures are recomputed from the new categorical distributions before the next tree. This repeated re-evaluation of the choice likelihood is what links discrete-choice estimation to gradient boosting.
Curvature convention. The exact categorical Hessian has off-diagonal terms linking alternatives of the same pass, whereas XGBoost takes one scalar per row. This scalar is a curvature convention for constructing trees. For the flat softmax the implemented convention is
\[
h_{ij}^{\mathrm{flat}}=\max\!\left\{\varepsilon,\frac{J_i}{J_i-1}\pi_{ij}(1-\pi_{ij})\right\},
\qquad J_i=|\mathcal G_i|.
\]
The factor \(J_i/(J_i-1)\) follows the RUMBoost reference implementation, (Salvadé and Hillel n.d.), and \(\varepsilon=10^{-6}\) keeps the curvature away from zero. For the CNL, the gradient is the exact gradient of the CNL choice likelihood and the scalar curvature reproduces the published RUMBoost f_obj_cross_nested convention. The implementation passes the reference curvature to XGBoost unchanged. The two models therefore share the boosting machinery and optimize different probability maps. The scalar curvature is a tree-fitting approximation, and the dependence among candidate destinations is retained by the likelihood and its gradient. At \(\mu=1\) the CNL probabilities and gradient reduce to the flat softmax, while the published CNL curvature convention differs numerically from the flat rule, so the boosting updates of the two models differ.
Dissimilarity update. The CNL learns \(\mu\) together with the trees. After every 20 trees, the utilities are held fixed. The fitting-set CE is evaluated at the current \(\rho\) and at \(1,1.5,2,3,5,10\); one bounded SLSQP optimization over \(\rho\in[1,10]\) starts from the best scanned value. Failed or uphill updates are rejected. This is a conditional scalar scan. Only 10% of the proposed move is applied, to avoid abrupt changes in the choice probabilities:
\[
\rho^{(t+1)}=\rho^{(t)}+0.1\bigl(\rho^*-\rho^{(t)}\bigr).
\]
Boosting then resumes with probabilities and derivatives recomputed at the new dissimilarity. Validation cross-entropy selects the joint checkpoint of tree ensemble and \(\mu\). This alternating scheme extends the RUMBoost cross-nested approach (Salvadé and Hillel 2024) to fixed pitch-control memberships and the shared PRESS XGBoost utility. The 20-tree interval and 10% damping follow the RUMBoost source implementation (Salvadé and Hillel n.d.), as recorded in the reference provenance. They are implementation choices of the estimation procedure. The scalar scan, shared scale bounds and fixed pitch-control memberships are PRESS-specific adaptations.

Both use learning rate 0.05, row and column subsampling 0.8, CPU histogram boosting, at most 2,000 trees and early-stopping patience 100. The screening used the fold-0 development partition once, and the selected settings are applied unchanged in every outer fold. Its validation matches are outer-test matches in other folds (see the scope of the development benchmark). These settings were fixed before the five-fold evaluation. There is one boosting trajectory per family/fold, initialized at zero utilities and \(\mu=1\).


Match-wise held-out evaluation
The selected configurations were evaluated on five match-disjoint 6 + 2 + 2 partitions:

Six training matches fit the XGBoost utilities and the upstream feature components (physical pass-risk and ball-drive parameters, xT smoothing, categorical vocabulary).
Two fixed validation matches select the tree checkpoint by early stopping on native choice CE, then fit a single temperature-scaling parameter with the selected trees and CNL dissimilarity held fixed. The same pair is used for both operations and stays fixed within that outer fold.
Two test matches are used only for performance evaluation.

Temperature scaling. The calibrated distribution is \(\pi_{ij}^{(T)}\propto \pi_{ij}^{1/T}\), as defined in the model vignette. The single scalar \(T\) minimizes the cross-entropy of the observed choices on the two validation matches. \(T>1\) flattens the distribution and \(T<1\) concentrates it. The fitted values are close to one in every fold (table below), and the gain in cross-entropy is small. The deployed flat model retains the temperature.
The six-match tree fit is evaluated directly on the test matches. Temperature scaling is applied to the final destination distribution (after nest aggregation for CNL), with utilities, dissimilarity and the selected tree prefix held fixed. It is fitted after the hyperparameter screening and early stopping.
Each of the 6,810 decisions appears exactly once among the pooled test predictions. Upstream physical fitting and calibration are documented in the pass-probability benchmark and ball-drive benchmark. The full-data deployment refit is described at the end.

After evaluation, the flat model was refitted on all ten matches with 1,444 trees (the median validation-selected count across folds) and the screening-selected hyperparameters. The deployment model uses full-data physical feature fits and smoothed xT. Its temperature, \(T=1.0132954379\), was estimated from reconstructed raw out-of-fold distributions.
